The tailwind component of the wind along a flight course

Source: R/dwn.R
tailwd.Rd

The part of the wind that blows along a course, positive for a tailwind, from which Hener (2022) builds the instrument of the landing direction at Frankfurt Airport: aircraft land westbound (course 250 degrees) unless the tailwind on that course exceeds 2.6 m/s, so the days of the eastbound approach, and which municipalities lie under the noise, follow from the wind.

Usage

tailwd(dir, spd, course = 250, by = NULL, agg = "max")

Arguments

dir

Wind directions in degrees (NA allowed).

spd

Wind speeds, one per direction, 0 or more (NA allowed).

course

The course flown, degrees clockwise from north.

by

NULL or the group of each reading.

agg

"max" or "mean": a group's value.

Value

Without by, the tailwind component of each reading; with by, a data frame, one row per group (sorted): by and tw (NA for a group without a reading).

Details

For wind from dir (degrees clockwise from north, where the wind blows from) at speed spd, the component along course is spd * cos(dir + 180 - course): "positive for tailwinds and negative for headwinds in the direction of the West25 landing approach", 0 for "no wind at all or if it is blowing exactly perpendicular to the runway (i.e., from 340 or 160 degrees)" (Hener 2022, sec. 3, for course = 250). With by (the day of hourly readings), each group gives one value: agg = "max", the paper's "daily maximum partial wind speed ... calculated from hourly wind data", or "mean". The instrument is then 1 for a municipality under the eastbound approach on a day whose tailwind exceeds 2.6 m/s, 1 for one under the westbound approach on a day whose tailwind is at most 2.6, and 0 otherwise (sec. 3; see ivfe() for the estimate).

References

Hener, T. (2022). Noise pollution and violent crime. Journal of Public Economics, 215, 104748. doi:10.1016/j.jpubeco.2022.104748

See also

windiv(), ivfe(), dwnexp()

Examples

# wind from the east (70 degrees) at 4 m/s is a 4 m/s tailwind westbound
tailwd(c(70, 340, 250), c(4, 4, 4))
#> [1]  4.000000e+00 -7.347881e-16 -4.000000e+00
# hourly readings to the daily maximum, then Hener's instrument for a
# municipality under the eastbound approach
tw <- tailwd(c(70, 90, 250, 260), c(3, 2, 5, 1), by = c(1, 1, 2, 2))
as.integer(tw$tw > 2.6)
#> [1] 1 0
